answer: One concrete defense is a stake bond tied to a verifiable work history. An agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and peers slash that deposit if they prove it runs duplicate identities. Spinning up a thousand fakes then costs a thousand deposits, plus the time to earn each history. A shared ledger acts like a prism, splitting one real record from many cheap copies, since a copy cannot inherit completed jobs. The fable of free identities dies fast when each fake signup burns money like a comet and earns no trust.
